What counts as a liquidation

A liquidation is a forced close: a leveraged position whose margin can no longer cover the maintenance requirement gets taken over and closed by the exchange's risk engine. The totals here aggregate reported liquidation orders across major derivatives venues over a rolling 24-hour window. Totals differ between trackers because exchange coverage and time windows differ — any single number is best read as a lower bound. Watch individual events print in real time on the live liquidations feed, see where the next clusters sit on the liquidation heatmap, or browse the dated daily recap archive.

Why these numbers matter

Liquidation totals are the cleanest read on how much leverage just left the market. Big totals on longs mark capitulation lows more often than tops; big totals on shorts fuel squeezes. The record table also shows the pattern: every entry is a macro surprise or a structural break, not a normal trading day — which is why traders watch the live number when volatility hits.

If you trade with leverage, know your own number before the market finds it: the liquidation calculator shows exactly where your position dies, and the paper trading terminal lets you feel a cascade with zero real money at stake.
